terms.meaning: a written rule that says what shape a piece of data must have
a setting that may be left out
a shape where every listed field is optional
a per-industry change to how one maturity gate is named or described

sections.name: File setup, AttrType, AttributeSpec, IndustryRole, GateOverride, IndustryConfig
sections.title: Shapes for industry settings
sections.what: Describes the building blocks an industry setup uses: attribute fields, roles, gate overrides, and the full industry setup. It also brings in the gate key type so overrides can only use valid gate names.
sections.why: Likely reason: one agreed shape lets each industry be written the same way. Reason not stated in the code for the exact fields.
sections.watch_out: A new field must be added here first, or the compiler will reject industry entries that use it.

sections.name: DEFAULT_ROLES
sections.title: Standard roles every industry starts with
sections.what: Defines the default list of eleven parties that can be attached to a project, such as owner, operator, developer, contractors, lenders and the regulator. Each industry starts with this list and can add its own roles on top.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared list avoids repeating the same roles in every industry entry.
sections.watch_out: Changing a key here changes it for every industry that copies this list, and saved project data may depend on the old key.

sections.name: GENERIC_SOURCE_ATTRS, DEFAULT_CONFIG
sections.title: Shared source-text fields and fallback settings
sections.what: Holds a reusable block of free-text fields that keep the original wording from source spreadsheets, such as region, full name and cost notes. It also defines the fallback settings used for any industry without its own entry: no extra fields, no fixed unit, and the standard roles.
sections.why: The file comment says these fields keep source information even when a number cannot be read cleanly during import.
sections.watch_out: Fallback settings apply silently to any industry name that is not in the main list, so a misspelled industry gets blank settings with no error.

sections.name: INDUSTRY_CONFIGS, getIndustryConfig, getIndustryRoles, getIndustryAttributes, getCapacityUnit (part 1)
sections.title: Settings for nuclear, dairy, LNG and renewables
sections.what: Gives each of these industries its own capacity label and unit, extra fields and extra roles. Nuclear and dairy also get custom wording for two maturity gates. Renewables has the longest field list, including report sections and a field for wind-specific structured text.
sections.why: Likely reason: each industry measures scale and reports different facts, so its fields are listed separately.
sections.watch_out: The wind text field is shown as structured sections, so its expected format must match what the display code reads; the reason for this link is not stated in the code.

sections.name: INDUSTRY_CONFIGS, getIndustryConfig, getIndustryRoles, getIndustryAttributes, getCapacityUnit (part 2)
sections.title: Settings for renewables end, EV batteries, data centers and oil and gas
sections.what: Finishes the renewables roles, then sets up EV battery cell capacity, data centers measured in IT load, and oil and gas. The oil and gas entry leaves its capacity unit blank on purpose and keeps planned and actual budgets as plain text.
sections.why: The file comment says a default unit would be stamped onto projects with mixed units, which would invent a unit the source does not give.
sections.watch_out: Because the oil and gas unit is blank, any display or calculation that expects a unit must handle an empty value.

sections.name: INDUSTRY_CONFIGS, getIndustryConfig, getIndustryRoles, getIndustryAttributes, getCapacityUnit (part 3)
sections.title: Settings for hydrogen, water, mining, lithium and gas power
sections.what: Gives hydrogen and water the shared fallback settings. Mining and lithium mining each get their own written-out field lists for site type, process route, contractor, funding and cost baseline. The gas power entry begins here and uses the shared fallback fields plus project-specific ones.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for keeping the two mining lists as separate full copies, though they differ slightly.
sections.watch_out: Editing a field in one of these lists does not reach the others, so the same field can drift apart across industries.

sections.name: INDUSTRY_CONFIGS, getIndustryConfig, getIndustryRoles, getIndustryAttributes, getCapacityUnit (part 4)
sections.title: Remaining industries and lookup helper functions
sections.what: Finishes the gas power entry, then sets up ports, aerospace and defense, and real estate, with real estate using a fixed list of site types. It ends with four helpers: one returns an industry's full settings and the others return only its roles, fields, or capacity unit.
sections.why: Likely reason: the helpers let the rest of the app read settings without knowing how the list is stored.
sections.watch_out: An unknown industry name returns the fallback settings without any error, so a typo looks like a valid but empty industry.

summary: Defines the shapes of the per-industry settings, such as the capacity unit, extra fields, roles, and changes to maturity gate wording, with the per-industry values not visible in this packet.
purpose: Gives one typed description of what an industry setup must contain, so every industry follows the same pattern.
why: Likely reason: one shared shape lets the app read any industry the same way. Reason for the full design not stated in the code.
how: The file first brings in the gate key type from the maturity file. It then declares small shapes for attributes, roles, and gate overrides, and combines them into one industry setup shape. The per-industry values and lookup functions are in lines not visible in this packet.
inputs: The visible part takes no runtime inputs. Other files supply industry data that fills these shapes.
outputs: Type definitions only in the visible part. No values are produced there.
risks: A wrong shape can stop the whole app from compiling. The industry values that follow were not visible, so they could not be checked.
debug: If a type error appears for an industry, check that its fields match these shapes and that gate override names match the gate list in the maturity file. Only lines 1 to 8 were reviewed.
